paperNotes.body: Reviewed from the PDF on 2026-04-09. This paper reports 483 players over 5 years, 1,019 total injuries, and injury rates per 1,000 exposure hours, with severity graded by days absent from training (minimal 1-3, mild 4-7, moderate 8-28, severe >28 days). Injuries were recorded by KFA medical staff using the AFC Daily Medical Report, but the paper still does not publish a clean explicit injury case definition. Leaving flagged for definition follow-up.

Reviewed from the PDF on 2026-04-09. This is a 4-year men's college soccer team study. It records team injuries and athlete-exposures, with exposure explicitly defined as one athlete participating in one practice or game regardless of duration, and reports injury rates per 1,000 exposures. Team totals were 9, 15, 10, and 7 injuries across the 4 study years, with total injury rates of 12.10, 15.92, 11.07, and 8.57 per 1,000 exposures. However, the paper does not state a clean explicit injury case definition, and the injury ascertainment/reporting source is not clearly identified beyond saying an in-season injury record was kept. Leaving flagged for definition/reporting-source follow-up.

apply.body: Retrospectively archived from extraction on 2026-07-27 after eligibility adjudication. Although the paper reports injuries and athlete-exposures, it does not state an explicit injury case definition and does not identify whether the in-season injury record was maintained by medical staff, an athletic trainer, coaching staff, or researchers. The existing extracted injury-definition value was an interpretation, not an explicit case definition stated by the paper. Abdel adjudicated the paper for exclusion. No linked full-text screening record existed, and none was created. Archived in extraction without creating a replacement full-text screening record. Adjudicated by AbdelRahman Babiker on 2026-07-27.

Retrospectively archived from extraction on 2026-07-27 after eligibility adjudication. The paper states that clinical diagnoses and injury-related absence duration were obtained from newspapers, magazines, newsletters and tabloids and/or club medical-staff reports. It does not identify which individual observations came from media versus medical staff. Abdel adjudicated the mixed and incompletely attributable reporting source for exclusion. No linked full-text screening record existed, and none was created. Archived in extraction without creating a replacement full-text screening record. Adjudicated by AbdelRahman Babiker on 2026-07-27.
